attempts.summary: Strong concept and mostly strong structure, but it needs one accuracy fix and a tighter ending before it is ready to render.
improvement_suggestions: Scene 008: replace "That gap is exactly sigma two" with something like "The leftover error is governed by the next singular value, sigma two" so you do not claim equality too strongly.
Scene 010: cut the final sentence in half; end on the diagram with one crisp line, such as "A = UDV^T is rotate, stretch, rotate — and those stretch axes are the best-fit directions."
Scene 007: remove one of the two restatements of rotate-stretch-rotate and keep only the visual replay, so the viewer learns from the motion instead of hearing the same summary twice.
Scene 003: shorten the Pythagoras explanation by a sentence or two and let the triangle animation do more work; right now it starts to read like a textbook proof rather than a discovery.

Scene 004: change "The line finally locks into place. This winning direction has a name" to a more visual reveal, because the viewer has already seen the line become special and does not need the extra verbal announcement.

criteria.name: learning_path
criteria.feedback: The video mostly follows one clear question: best line, then best directions, then matrix action, then low-rank approximation, then payoff. It does introduce the core ideas in the right order with the running example, but scene 003-004 still sound a bit proof-like and abstract before the viewer has fully internalized the geometric picture.

criteria.name: accuracy
criteria.feedback: Most of the geometry is right, but one claim is overstated: "That gap is exactly sigma two" in scene 008 is not true as stated for the running example, and the line "those stretch directions are the exact same best-fit line we went looking for at the very start" blurs a 1D best-fit direction with the singular-vector directions of the matrix. Improvement: say the residual error is controlled by the next singular value, not that it is literally the gap.

criteria.name: narration_economy
criteria.feedback: The narration is generally lean, but several scenes repeat the same idea in slightly different words, especially scene 007 and scene 010. The ending also restates the thesis multiple times instead of landing once and stopping.

criteria.name: visual_design
criteria.feedback: The plan uses the core motifs consistently and every manim scene has motion, so it is visually coherent. However, the presenter scenes interrupt the motion, and some scenes rely on labels and arrows heavily enough that the visual interest risks flattening into exposition.

criteria.name: hook_and_payoff
criteria.feedback: The opening poses a concrete question about a cloud of points and a best line, which is a strong hook. The final scene does answer that question, but it lingers a little too long instead of stopping cleanly once the equivalence is made.

criteria.name: source_coverage
criteria.feedback: It covers the main geometric arc of the source well: best fit, singular vectors, SVD geometry, and best rank-k approximation. It deliberately leaves out the proof machinery and numerical method details, which is fine for the length.
